chunks: And a group narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, who said: Abu Muhammad Ammar ibn al-Husayn ibn Ishaq al-Asruushini narrated to us, who said: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi Salih al-Khujandi narrated to us

who had been persistent in investigation and seeking, traveled through the lands, and wrote via the hand of Sheikh Abu al-Qasim ibn Ruh (may Allah be pleased with him) to the Master (the Imam), complaining about his heart's attachment and preoccupation with investigation and seeking, asking for a reply that would bring peace to his soul, and revealing to him what he was doing.

He said: An epistle was issued to me, its text being: 'Whoever searches, he seeks; and whoever seeks, he leads on [my enemies]; and whoever leads on, he is like one who worships a deity other than Allah; and whoever worships a deity other than Allah, he associates partners with Allah.'
He said: So I ceased from seeking, my soul found peace, and I returned to my hometown happy, and all praise is to Allah.

key_terms.أَشَاطَ: To lead on or guide (enemies to the Imam)
key_terms.تَوْقِيع: Epistle or handwritten letter from the Imam
key_terms.ذَلَّ: To be led on or humbled (in the context of enemies finding him)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Imam's epistle regarding the consequences of seeking his location?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the theological principle that excessive curiosity regarding the Imam's physical location during the Minor Occultation (*al-Ghayb al-Sughra*) can lead to spiritual deviation. The chain of consequences—searching, seeking, being led astray, and ultimately associating partners with God—underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Imam's hiddenness is a divine test of faith rather than a mere absence. Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Khujandi’s immediate cessation of his search illustrates the practical application of accepting divine wisdom over intellectual pursuit.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 271 - Narrated to me a group of scholars from Muhammad bin Ali Husain that he said: Narrated to us Abu Muhammad Ammar bin Husain bin Ishaq Usrooshini that: Narrated to us Abul Abbas Ahmad bin Hasan bin Abi Salih Khujandi that: “

After he had been fascinated with the search and investigation into the matter of Imamate after the Eleventh Imam and had left his homeland to find out what to do. He also wrote a letter to the Master of the Time (a.s), through Husain Ibn Rauh complaining about his bewilderment as it had affected his whole life and begged for a reply, which would accord him comfort and peace of heart.

He himself says: An epistle was issued to me from Imam (a.s): ‘Whoever searches, he seeks; and whoever seeks, he leads [my enemies] on [and divulges my location to people]; and whoever leads on, [it is as if] he destroys [me]; and whoever destroys [me], [it is as if] he worships a deity other than Allah.’
On seeing that epistle I gave up the search, my heart got peace and I returned to my hometown happily, thanks be to Allah.
